name: Question 15
worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-5$ and $\sigma =\sqrt{16}=4.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.64<X<3.64) & =P(\frac{0.64-5}{4}<Z<\frac{3.64-5}{4}) \\  & =P(-1.09<Z<-0.34)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/6c919bfe71b67ed94751cb53bd5f24e9e80e7979a28a8e28b123aac907d6b7e4.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.09<Z<-0.34) & =P(Z<-0.34)-P(Z\le -1.09) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.34)-P(Z\le -1.09) \\  & =Φ(-0.34)-Φ(-1.09)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.34) & =0.3669 \\ Φ(-1.09) & =0.1379\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.09<Z<-0.34) & =Φ(-0.34)-Φ(-1.09) \\  & =0.3669-0.1379 \\  & =0.2290.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(0.64<X<3.64)=0.2290.
$$

EXPLANATION

Given a normal random variable X∼N(μ,σ2), we have

P(a<X<b)=P(a−μσ<Z<b−μσ)

where Z∼N(0,1) is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have μ=−5 and σ=16=4.

First, we transform X into a standard normal random variable Z by z-scoring:

P(0.64<X<3.64)=P(0.64−54<Z<3.64−54)=P(−1.09<Z<−0.34)

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of Φ(z):

P(−1.09<Z<−0.34)=P(Z<−0.34)−P(Z≤−1.09)=P(Z≤−0.34)−P(Z≤−1.09)=Φ(−0.34)−Φ(−1.09)

From the table, we have the following:

Φ(−0.34)=0.3669Φ(−1.09)=0.1379

Therefore, we have

P(−1.09<Z<−0.34)=Φ(−0.34)−Φ(−1.09)=0.3669−0.1379=0.2290.

Finally, we conclude that

P(0.64<X<3.64)=0.2290.
